pages.text: Today was Amina’s first day at school. She put on her new blue and white uniform. Her tummy felt funny, like butterflies were dancing inside.
sentences: Today was Amina’s first day at school.
She put on her new blue and white uniform.
Her tummy felt funny, like butterflies were dancing inside.
pages.alt: A girl in a new school uniform stands by a mirror holding her tummy, looking nervous but smiling a little.

pages.text: Mama held her hand all the way to school. ‘It is okay to feel nervous,’ said Mama. ‘Everybody feels that way on a first day.’
sentences: Mama held her hand all the way to school.
‘It is okay to feel nervous,’ said Mama.
‘Everybody feels that way on a first day.’
pages.alt: Amina walks to school holding her mother’s hand along a sunny road.

pages.text: At the gate, a bell went ding-dong! Children ran in from every side. Amina’s feet did not want to move. ‘I do not want to go in,’ she whispered.
sentences: At the gate, a bell went ding-dong!
Children ran in from every side.
Amina’s feet did not want to move.
‘I do not want to go in,’ she whispered.
pages.alt: A busy school gate with children running in; Amina stands still holding her backpack straps.

pages.text: A smiling teacher came to the gate. ‘Good morning, Amina. I am Madam Abena. We have been waiting for you.’ She knelt down so that they were eye to eye.
sentences: A smiling teacher came to the gate.
‘Good morning, Amina.
I am Madam Abena.
We have been waiting for you.’ She knelt down so that they were eye to eye.
pages.alt: A friendly teacher kneels at the school gate to speak to Amina at her height.

pages.text: In the classroom, Amina sat down next to a boy named Salifu. ‘Do you like crayons?’ he asked. ‘I have a red one, a blue one and a yellow one.’
sentences: In the classroom, Amina sat down next to a boy named Salifu.
‘Do you like crayons?’ he asked.
‘I have a red one, a blue one and a yellow one.’
pages.alt: Two children sit at a shared desk; the boy holds out three crayons.

pages.text: Amina took the yellow crayon and drew a big sun. Salifu drew a tree. Soon the butterflies in her tummy were quiet.
sentences: Amina took the yellow crayon and drew a big sun.
Salifu drew a tree.
Soon the butterflies in her tummy were quiet.
pages.alt: The two children draw a sun and a tree together on one sheet of paper.

pages.text: At break time, Amina and Salifu played a clapping game with the other children. Amina laughed so much that she forgot she had been nervous.
sentences: At break time, Amina and Salifu played a clapping game with the other children.
Amina laughed so much that she forgot she had been nervous.
pages.alt: A group of children play a clapping game in the school yard, Amina laughing.

pages.text: When school ended, Mama was waiting at the gate. ‘How was your first day?’ she asked. Amina smiled. ‘I made a friend, and I will go again tomorrow!’ The end.
sentences: When school ended, Mama was waiting at the gate.
‘How was your first day?’ she asked.
Amina smiled.
‘I made a friend, and I will go again tomorrow!’ The end.
pages.alt: Amina runs to her mother at the gate, smiling and waving a drawing.

activities.question: How did Amina feel at the school gate?
activities.explanation: Her feet did not want to move and she whispered that she did not want to go in.

items: Madam Abena met Amina at the gate.
Amina and Salifu drew a picture.
